hpi: {{patient_name}} is a 19-year-old sexually active man who presents with dysuria, fevers, and chills. Rectal exam reveals an edematous, tender prostate — the key finding that localizes the infection to the prostate rather than the bladder or urethra alone. He denies flank pain or CVA tenderness (making pyelonephritis less likely). The differential includes cystitis, urethritis, pyelonephritis, and sexually transmitted infections (Chlamydia, gonorrhea). E. coli accounts for approximately one-third of prostatitis cases. Fluoroquinolones are the treatment of choice due to their ability to penetrate the inflamed prostate.

physical_exam: Suprapubic tenderness may be present. No CVA tenderness (rules out pyelonephritis).
Dysuria. Urethral discharge absent. Testicular exam normal.
Edematous, tender prostate on digital rectal exam — pathognomonic for prostatitis. CAUTION: do not perform vigorous prostate massage — risk of bacteremia.

case_summary: Acute bacterial prostatitis in sexually active 19-year-old. DRE: tender, edematous prostate. Urine gram stain: gram-negative rods (E. coli). UA + urine culture + STI panel + CBC → ciprofloxacin 14-28 days. Office management. Prevention: Tdap, meningococcal vaccine, safe sex counseling.
